historical_references.reference: Jharna was the name of a river in ancient India, mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. It is described as a tributary that flows into the Saraswati river. The reference is in the Bhagavad Gita, where Krishna speaks of the divine existence of rivers, including the Jharna.

The name Jharna is also mentioned in the Puranic literature as the name of a celestial river in the heavens, flowing from the feet of Lord Shiva and joining the river Ganga. This is described in the Shiva Purana and other similar texts.
